title: Flatness comparison of a chart stalk and its closed fibre
statement: Let T be affine, f:X→T flat and locally finitely presented, and U an affine open of X [def-weil-flat-morphism; def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let e:U→A^n_T be locally finitely presented with projection f|U [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. For x∈U the chart stalk map is flat if and only if the canonical polynomial closed-fibre stalk map φ is flat [lem-sbc-polynomial-chart-canonical-fibre-stalk; def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No quasi-finiteness assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 00RH, application of the local criterion in Tag 00R7; arbitrary base rings allowed.

proof.text: Put A=O_T,p, P=O_AffineSpace,e(x), B=O_U,x. The factorization gives a local tower A→P→B. Polynomial finite presentation and local finite presentation of f imply that P and B are essentially finitely presented over A. B as a B-module is nonzero and finitely presented, and is flat over A because the restriction of f to U is flat. Identify P/m_A P and B/m_A B with the polynomial fibre stalk and open fibre stalk using stalk localization and residue-field base change. Transport the latter through the open fibre inclusion to S. Under these compatible identifications the quotient map is the canonical φ.

Flatness of the P→B map implies flatness of its closed fibre map by base change and localization. Conversely apply the local flatness fibre criterion to the tower A→P→B with M=B: all hypotheses were checked in the first step and the closed fibre module is flat precisely when φ is flat. Ring isomorphisms preserve flatness, giving the claimed equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem polynomial_chart_stalk_flat_comparison
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (f : X ⟶ T)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (U : X.Opens) [IsAffine U.toScheme] (n : ℕ)
    (e : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation e]
    (he : e ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) T ↘ T) = U.ι ≫ f)
    (x : U.toScheme) :
    (e.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ↔ (PolynomialChart.stalkMap f U n e he x).Flat
